draft.title: What a biome is
card: A biome is a large region of the world where the climate, soils, plants and animals are similar. Tropical rainforest and desert are two examples.
Climate sets the pattern. Temperature and rainfall decide which plants can grow, and those plants decide which animals can live there.
Soils are part of a biome too. Plants and animals live in the soil, and the soil in turn is shaped by the plants that grow in it.
A biome is not one country or one farm. Places far apart, such as the Amazon and the Congo basin, can belong to the same biome if they share these features.
draft.remember: A biome is a big region defined by its shared climate, soils, plants and animals.

a.q: Which description best fits a biome?
opts: A large region with a similar climate, soils and life
A region whose borders are set by a country's government
A single group of animals that share the same food source
A farm area where one crop is grown across many seasons
a.why: A biome is defined by shared climate, soils, plants and animals over a large region. Borders drawn by governments do not decide a biome, because the same biome can cross many countries.
a.clue: Think about what the living and non-living features have in common.

b.q: Two rainforests, one in Brazil and one in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, are on different continents. Why can both be the same biome?
opts: They share a similar climate, soils, plants and animals
They are both inside the same country's borders
They have exactly the same species of plants and animals
They are both close to each other on the same continent
b.why: A biome is grouped by similar features, not by place or by matching species. Both rainforests are hot and wet with similar types of plants and animals, so they are the same biome even though they are far apart and have different species.
b.clue: Biomes are grouped by what places are like, not where they are.

a.best: A large region with a similar climate, soils and life

b.best: They share a similar climate, soils, plants and animals

b.q: A geographer says a rainforest in Brazil and a rainforest in the Democratic Republic of the Congo are the same biome. What is the best reason?
opts: They share a similar climate, soils, plants and animals
They contain exactly the same species of plants and animals
They are both protected by law as national parks or reserves
They each cover about the same total area of land
b.why: A biome is grouped by similar features. Both rainforests are hot and wet, with similar kinds of plants and animals, so they are the same biome. They do not need the same species, and their size or legal protection does not decide the biome.
